strengths: A very relevant problem being investigated.
The method proposed makes sense and is simple.
The analysis on dataset size and noise was nice to see, and not common in existing literature to my knowledge.
The derivations for the linear approximations for the distribution of positions is also useful.
The proposed model beats the baseline model.
This paper shows some performance improvement over the MTR model on the WOD dataset.
weaknesses: Novelty is very limited, as the authors present a method of an existing work that is not referenced.
Writing and explanations can be improved.
Experiments are quite dry and could be expanded with more visualizations.
"but also scales well in size", unclear if this is a good or a bad thing; the authors should clarify this better.

The authors need to cite the earlier work listed above, and put their work into context; this is the biggest issue with the current manuscript and makes the work not ready for publication until this is done (since the level of contributions of the work is questionable).
Figures 1 and 2 are not referenced in the text.
Notation can be improved; e.g., in the equation for L in Section 4.1 the notation p_h is not introduced before being used. The authors should make sure that all notation is properly defined.
"we downscale the model", how exactly? Unclear.
The authors do not properly explain the experiments, such as the number of mixture components used and other information relevant to understanding the approach and the experiments.
For the experiments with noisy trajectories, do you add noise during training as well? Unclear, would be good to clarify.
The paper is missing many related works that have explored kinematic priors for trajectory forecasting and should more clearly position its work in the context of existing literature.
It is unclear whether the authors compare to the original MTR or a re-implemented version, and absolute numbers for the baseline are missing.
Results are reported only relative to the baseline, lacking absolute performance numbers needed to assess whether gains hold when scaling the model.

The authors claim that previous state-of-the-art results were only obtained by directly predicting Euclidean coordinates, but existing works such as MULTIPATH++ also use an underlying kinematics model, contradicting this claim.
Lack of novelty/contributions; trajectory forecasting with kinematics models exists in literature, and the given kinematic model derivations are quite straightforward.

The contribution of this paper is very weak; the related work section incorrectly claims that none of the existing trajectory works uses the bicycle kinematic model, despite many models (e.g., MultiPath++ [1] and DKM [2]) that explicitly use it.
None of the three proposed formulations used the actual bicycle kinematic model; Formulation 1, which performs best, simply predicts deltas between waypoints.

The evaluation results lack important information; tables only show relative improvement from the MTR baseline without clarifying whether the MTR numbers are from the original paper, the WOD leaderboard, or the authors' own implementation.
Please add equation numbers.
The expression sigma_{x + vx * dt} = sigma_x + sigma_{vx} * dt is likely incorrect; the correct summation of two Gaussian variables should be sigma_{x + y} = sqrt(sigma_x^2 + sigma_y^2).
Reference Chai et al., 2020a and Chai et al., 2020b are the same paper.
